name: CHZ Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The CHZ's top belt, first won by Millenium in a four-man elimination battle royal at Caged Fury 1 on 1 August 1999. Its own title history carries it through the fed's years as the FWF and the SWF — Cellrock relinquishing it when the CHZ closed in November 1999, JT Fringe winning the FWF title at that fed's opening, Rufus Blaq becoming the first SWF World Champion — and through a six-month vacancy while the SWF was closed in 2000. Kris Snyder, later Chazzy 2 Cool, won it in the New CHZ on 27 May 2001; Staz took it from him on 4 July and left North America with the belt at the end of August. After five months vacant, Matt "The Franchise" Helms won it at Caged Fury 2 on 30 January 2002, beating Diablo and then Don Rossi, The Count and Chazzy 2 Cool in a two-cage final, and is billed to defend it against Keyser Soze at NBK Pride, with no result surviving. The fed's June 2002 relaunch under a new owner listed a World Heavyweight Championship with no champions and crowned its own first champion (see chz-world-heavyweight). The belt's 2003 shows, after the fed's new era opened at BreakOut 2002: Gus Theo is billed champion on 5 March 2003, Matt Helms holds it again by 26 March after Caged Fury 2, and Harry Manback beat Helms for it at May HayDay 2 on 14 May 2003, keeping it on 21 May when a second referee's count of Drayton MacPhereson was ruled void.
notes: The chain follows the fed's own Heavyweight title history (/promotions/chz/archive/heavyweight-title-history.html), which runs through the fed's FWF and SWF years exactly as the fed kept it; the Hall of Fame, the news archive and the held show scripts corroborate it. The 2003 reigns are filed on this belt, not on the June 2002 relaunch's (chz-world-heavyweight): the new era that opened at BreakOut 2002 carried the fed's 2001-02 belts on (Don Rossi, North American champion since February 2002, defends that title at BreakOut, "A title mind you that Don Rossi held twice before", /promotions/chz/archive/breakout-2002-12-18.html; Mad Max, Hardcore champion since March 2002, defends it on 26 March 2003), and on 26 March 2003 Matt Helms, this belt's champion of January 2002, says "Not only do I once again possess the CHZ World title" (/promotions/chz/archive/wnw-2003-03-26.html).

name: CHZ Intercontinental Championship
epitaph: Cellrock was the first CHZ Intercontinental Champion, beating Triple D in a Last Man Standing match at Caged Fury 1 on 1 August 1999 and winning fifteen straight before the CHZ closed. The belt ran on through the FWF and SWF years — Kryptosonic, who retired undefeated; JT Fringe and Jaguar-F trading it in February 2000; Staz ending Jaguar-F's career in a Loser Leaves Town cage match. In the New CHZ, Black Dragon, Don Rossi and Merlin held it through 2001; Chazzy 2 Cool took it from Merlin on 12 December 2001, Brent Brewer from Chazzy 2 Cool on 9 January 2002, and Kaanen Thorne from Brewer on 18 March 2002. Thorne is billed to defend it in a three-way at NBK Pride, with no result surviving.
notes: The fed's own Intercontinental title history (/promotions/chz/archive/intercontinental-title-history.html) dates every change from 1999; Brewer won the title from Chazzy 2 Cool on 9 January 2002.

name: CHZ North American Championship
epitaph: Created in the New CHZ in 2001: Don Rossi won it on 2 May 2001, beating Chester Park in the final, and lost it three weeks later to Thor. Steve Santos made Thor submit for it in July and kept it through the autumn shows, against Gazz Maybury on 21 September and Matt Helms on 9 November, until he retired; Matt Helms won it from Brian Nash at the 12 December 2001 Wild and lost it to Violent Dave on 9 January 2002; Rossi took it back from Dave on 6 February 2002, the first two-time champion. Rossi retains it against Diablo by disqualification on 22 March 2002 and is billed to defend it again at NBK Pride, with no result surviving. Rob Lewis beat Don Rossi for it at BreakOut 2002 on 18 December 2002; Lucifer is billed its champion on 5 March 2003, when he does not come to work for a defence against Bloodlust, and Keyser Soze was its champion by 26 March 2003 and kept it through a count-out loss to Chris Holler on 9 April.
notes: The fed's own North American title history (/promotions/chz/archive/north-american-title-history.html): Santos lost it to Matt Helms on 21 September 2001; Violent Dave took it from Helms on 11 January 2002 and Rossi from Dave on 6 February 2002.

name: CHZ Hardcore Championship
epitaph: The Count won the first CHZ Hardcore Championship at Caged Fury 1 on 1 August 1999, in the match since named the Transylvania Hardcore Match, and carried it through the CHZ and FWF mergers. The SWF years passed it among Staz, Freddy Landstrom, the Outlawz and BlaQ Inc.; The Count won it twice more and was kept as a non-fighting champion until the New CHZ held a final, which Diablo won over his partner Fire on 21 September 2001. Extreme Chancelz took it from Diablo in the fed's first barbed wire match, 14 November 2001; Black Dragon, Lucifer and Madd Maxx followed in early 2002, Maxx winning it on 6 March 2002 and billed to defend it against Wild Dog and Lucifer at NBK Pride, with no result surviving. Lucifer beat Mad Max for it on 26 March 2003; Xear was champion by 23 April, and Zen Kyosaku beat him for it in a three-way at May HayDay 2 on 14 May 2003.
notes: The fed's own Hardcore title history (/promotions/chz/archive/hardcore-title-history.html): Black Dragon took it from Extreme Chancelz on 24 January 2002, Lucifer from Black Dragon at No Luv on 27 February, and Madd Maxx from Lucifer on 6 March 2002. The 21 September 2001 Friday Night Wild bills Diablo's win "for the right to be the First Hardcore Champion" and calls him "the first ever CHZ hardcore champion" (/promotions/chz/archive/fnw-2001-09-21.html), where the title history carries the belt back to The Count on 1 August 1999: sources disagree.

name: CHZ Tag Team Championship
epitaph: Millennium and Canon, the original Outlawz, were its first champions at Caged Fury 1 on 1 August 1999; Sex and Violence — Dirk Diggler and The Crow — won it five times across the CHZ, FWF and SWF years, trading it with the Detroit Boyz in the autumn of 1999 and retiring after their last reign in 2000. Boylan's Boys held it longest, from November 2000 to May 2001. In the New CHZ the Disciples of Thunder held it from May 2001 and Hell's Fury (Diablo and Fire) from July; Son's of Thunder (James and John, managed by Simon) won it from Hell's Fury in the fed's first tables match on 9 November 2001, and by 23 January 2002 the Disciples (Atlas and Mountain) are billed the reigning champions, with no show recording the change. The Disciples were fired and the titles went vacant on 1 March 2002, and the Midnight Wonders won them in a four-corners elimination match on the 13 March 2002 Wild; they are billed to defend against Soul Stormer and 'Psycho' Cody Hawk at NBK Pride, with no result surviving. The fed's June 2002 relaunch under a new owner listed a Tag Team Championship with no champions and crowned its own champions (see chz-tag-team-2002). The titles were reinstated in 2003 after a tournament to crown new winners: the AAOD, Lucifer and Diablo, won them by beating the Reaper and Archangel, billed Heaven and Hell, at May HayDay 2 on 14 May 2003 and kept them on 21 May.
notes: The fed's own Tag Team title history (/promotions/chz/archive/tag-team-title-history.html) gives the Disciples of Thunder (2) one reign, 9 November 2001 to 1 March 2002 ("DOT was fired after a period of inactivity"), and dates the Midnight Wonders' win 18 March 2002; the 9 November 2001 Friday Night Wild crowns the Sons of Thunder and the 13 March 2002 Wild stages the four-corners match. Sources disagree. The 2003 reign is filed on this belt, not on the June 2002 relaunch's (chz-tag-team-2002): the new era that opened at BreakOut 2002 carried the fed's 2001-02 belts on (see chz-heavyweight's notes), and the 14 May 2003 booth calls the titles "reinstated" (/promotions/chz/archive/may-hayday-2-2003-05-14.html).

name: CHZ Television Championship
epitaph: Established in 2002 and decided by an eight-man, three-week tournament: Chris Nightly won the final at No Luv on 27 February 2002, and he changed his name to Chris Mathews on 1 March, which the fed's own title history counted as a second reign, "the shortest title rain ever," though the title did not change hands. Rage tapped Mathews out with an ankle lock on 22 March 2002 to take it, and is billed to defend it against Galuda at NBK Pride, with no result surviving.
notes: The fed's own Television title history (/promotions/chz/archive/television-title-history.html) records the tournament win at No Luv, 27 February 2002, as Chris Nightly, and his renaming to Chris Mathews on 1 March 2002 as a second reign.

name: CHZ National Championship
epitaph: The secondary singles title of the CHZ's 2002 run, decided by a tournament that opened on the first Wild in July 2002. Xander Crave won it from Logan Cage on 7 August 2002 and kept it through the summer, against Tyler Van Serio on 21 August and Logan Cage again in a knockout match at Mind Games, until the fed's new owner stripped every champion on 11 September 2002.
notes: Named on the fed's own 2002 champions and title-history pages (/promotions/chz/archive/champions-2002-09.html; /promotions/chz/archive/title-history-2002.html); not one of the belts the fed's 2001-02 site listed.

name: CHZ Women's Championship
epitaph: Introduced at BreakOut 2002 on 18 December 2002 as a golden-thong belt made for the event, which Xstacy won by beating Misty Helms with Mad Max's help. Commissioner Inferno stripped her of it on 23 April 2003 after the belt she swung at Sai hit him, and Sai, managed by Dynamo Dragon, won the vacant title by beating Misty Helms at May HayDay 2 on 14 May 2003.

name: CHZ Omega Championship
epitaph: A title the booth calls one carried over to the CHZ from the LOW, which Inferno won by beating Lucifer in a TLC cage match at BreakOut 2002 on 18 December 2002. Wild Dog was declared Omega Champion after beating Gus Theo on 26 March 2003 and kept it by disqualification against Lucifer on 9 April; with the title vacant, he won it again by beating Chazy 2 Cool in a ladder match at May HayDay 2 on 14 May 2003.

name: CHZ Alpha Championship
epitaph: Harry Manback is the Alpha Champion at BreakOut 2002 on 18 December 2002, when Petapaw names a number one contender for the belt. Don Rossi won it on 26 March 2003 and the Darkness took it from him at May HayDay 2 on 14 May, handing it over that night to Rage, whom Keyser Soze named the nBk's Alpha Champion.

name: CHZ World Heavyweight Championship
epitaph: The belt of the CHZ's June 2002 relaunch under its new owner, listed on the fed's title page with no champions and on its champions page as vacant, the contenders to be announced. Jake Schultz was crowned "the first CHZ World Heavyweight Champion" at Mind Games on 31 August 2002, powerbombing Matt Hunt through a table in a barbed wire tables match, and lost it when the fed's new owner stripped every champion on 11 September 2002.
notes: Named on the fed's own 2002 champions and title-history pages (/promotions/chz/archive/champions-2002-06.html; /promotions/chz/archive/title-history-2002.html) and billed "the first CHZ World Heavyweight Champion" on its 11 September 2002 front page (/promotions/chz/archive/front-page-2002-09.html). The 2003 World title is filed on chz-heavyweight (see its notes).

name: CHZ Tag Team Championship (2002)
epitaph: The Tag Team belt of the CHZ's June 2002 relaunch under its new owner, listed on the fed's title page with no champions and on its champions page as vacant, the contenders to be announced. A tag team title tournament ended on 14 August 2002 with Redemption Song, Jim Surge and Ben Campbell, beating the Flying Vergomovs in a falls count anywhere final; they kept the titles against Gold Rush on 21 August, the Mind Games cage match against the Mystery Assailants ended in a no contest, and the fed declared the titles vacant on 2 September 2002 as Redemption Song moved on.
notes: Named on the fed's own 2002 champions and title-history pages (/promotions/chz/archive/champions-2002-06.html; /promotions/chz/archive/title-history-2002.html); not the belt of the fed's own 2001-02 Tag Team title history (/promotions/chz/archive/tag-team-title-history.html). The Tag Team titles reinstated in 2003 are filed on chz-tag-team, the belt that era carried on (see its notes).
